extracted.intended_audience: investment advisers, compliance officers, and legal counsel for investment advisers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements for registration, exemptions, filings, and definitions applicable to SEC investment advisers and private fund advisers. Covers Form ADV/ADV-NR/ADV-W/ADV-H procedures, eligibility thresholds, definitions (client, investor, assets under management), and related exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single client safe harbor (section 202(a)(30))
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists persons and arrangements that may be treated as a single client for purposes of section 202(a)(30) of the Act, including: (i) a natural person and certain family members and spousal equivalents; (ii) a corporation, partnership, LLC, trust (with caveats) where the natural person and/or persons referred are the only primary beneficiaries; (iii) legal organizations advised based on the organization's investment objectives rather than individual owners' objectives; and (iv) two or more legal organizations with identical owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph is a safe harbor and not intended to be exclusive. Includes examples (natural person + spouse/spousal equivalent, trusts where natural person(s) are only primary beneficiaries) and clarifies that 'legal organization' treated as a single client when advice is based on the entity's objectives, not individual owners'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules regarding counting clients (owners and private funds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules clarifying when an owner of a legal organization must be counted as a client: (1) you must count an owner as a client if you provide investment advisory services to the owner separate and apart from services to the legal organization; (2) you are not required to count an owner solely because you offer, promote, or sell interests in the legal organization to the owner or report periodically to owners as a group; (3) a limited partnership or LLC is a client of any general partner, managing member or other person acting as adviser to it; (4) you need not count a private fund as a client if you count an investor (per paragraph (c)(2)) in that private fund as an investor in the United States; (5) you need not count a person as an investor in a private fund if you count such person as a client in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides operational clarifications intended to prevent double-counting and to define when owners vs. entities should be treated as clients for counting purposes. Emphasizes limited circumstances where an owner is not automatically a client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assets under management definition
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Assets under management’ means the regulatory assets under management as determined under Item 5.F of Form ADV (§ 279.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout threshold calculations (e.g., eligibility for SEC registration, exemptions). Later sections provide exclusions to this definition for particular exemptions (e.g., private fund adviser exemption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor definition (for private fund rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Investor’ means (i) any person who would be included in determining the number of beneficial owners of outstanding securities of a private fund under section 3(c)(1) or whether outstanding securities are owned exclusively by qualified purchasers under section 3(c)(7), and (ii) any beneficial owner of any outstanding short-term paper issued by the private fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: You may treat as a single investor any person who is an investor in two or more private funds you advise.

rubrics_metrics.name: In the United States — definition for client/investor location
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘In the United States’ means, with respect to any client or investor: (i) any person who is a U.S. person as defined in § 230.902(k), except that any discretionary or similar account held for the benefit of a person in the United States by a dealer or other professional fiduciary is in the United States if the dealer or fiduciary is a related person of the adviser and is not organized/incorporated/resident in the United States; (ii) any place of business in the United States (per § 230.902(l)); and (iii) the public in the United States (per § 230.902(l)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: A person who is in the United States may be treated as not being in the United States if such person was not in the U.S. at the time of becoming a client or, for investors, each time the investor acquires securities issued by the fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place of business and spousal equivalent cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Place of business’ has the same meaning as in § 275.222-1(a). ‘Spousal equivalent’ has the same meaning as in § 275.202(a)(11)(G)-1(d)(9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References provide consistent definitions used for determining client counts, place-of-business tests, and family aggregation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding out — participation in non-public private fund offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: If relying on the single client safe harbor, you shall not be deemed to be holding yourself out generally to the public in the United States as an investment adviser solely because you participate in a non-public offering in the United States of securities issued by a private fund under the Securities Act of 1933.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits a circumstance that might otherwise be viewed as public solicitation; designed to allow private fund offerings without constituting general holding out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form ADV initial registration filing requirements (§ 275.203-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply for Commission registration as an investment adviser you must complete Form ADV by following its instructions and file Part 1A of Form ADV, the firm brochure(s) required by Part 2A, and Form CRS required by Part 3 electronically with the IARD unless you have a hardship exemption under § 275.203-3. You are not required to file brochure supplements required by Part 2B. If you are not required to deliver a brochure or Form CRS to any clients, you are not required to prepare or file them with the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note regarding availability of IARD filing information on SEC website. Transition dates: on or after June 30, 2020, initial applications must include a Form CRS satisfying Part 3; initial applications filed prior to June 30, 2020 had to include compliant Form CRS by June 30, 2020.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Form ADV is considered filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Form ADV is considered filed with the Commission upon acceptance by the IARD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational rule for determining filing date and hence timing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form ADV filing fees
rubrics_metrics.description: You must pay FINRA (IARD operator) a filing fee. The Commission has approved the amount. No portion of the filing fee is refundable. Your completed application will not be accepted by FINRA (and thus not filed with the Commission) until you have paid the filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-payment prevents acceptance and filing; fees are non-refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form ADV-NR (non-resident) filing and amendment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each non-resident general partner or non-resident managing agent of any investment adviser registered or applying for registration must submit Form ADV-NR in connection with initial registration; if a person becomes a non-resident general partner/agent after initial filing, they must file ADV-NR within 30 days. Amendments required within 30 days whenever information becomes inaccurate. ADV-NR must be filed electronically via IARD unless hardship exemption granted. Form ADV-NR is considered filed upon IARD acceptance. No fee required. ADV-NR is a 'report' under sections 204 and 207.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies timing, electronic filing, amendment deadlines, and the report status of ADV-NR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form ADV-W withdrawal procedures and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: You must file Form ADV-W to withdraw from investment adviser registration (or withdraw a pending application). Once you have electronically filed your Form ADV (or amendments) with IARD, any ADV-W you file must be filed with IARD unless you have a hardship exemption. Each ADV-W is effective upon IARD acceptance, but registration continues for 60 days after acceptance solely for the purpose of commencing a proceeding under section 203(e) of the Act. No fee to file ADV-W through IARD. ADV-W is a 'report' under sections 204 and 207.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies electronic filing requirement, effective date, residual registration period for legal proceedings, no fee, and report classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardship exemptions for electronic filing (temporary and continuing) (§ 275.203-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides two hardship exemptions from electronic filing requirements: (a) Temporary hardship — eligible if registered or registering and have unanticipated technical difficulties preventing IARD submission; to request: file Form ADV-H in paper no later than one business day after the filing was due and submit the subject filing electronically within seven business days; exemption effective upon filing of a completed ADV-H. (b) Continuing hardship — available to ‘small businesses’; must file ADV-H at least ten business days before a filing is due; Commission will grant/deny within ten business days; exemption effective upon approval; period no longer than one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing hardship grants require demonstration that electronic filing requirements are prohibitively burdensome or expensive. Small business defined by Item 12 responses on Form ADV. FINRA will charge an additional fee to convert paper filings submitted under continuing hardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venture capital fund definition and qualifying criteria (§ 275.203(l)-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of section 203(l), a venture capital fund is an entity described in certain subparagraphs of the Act or any private fund that: (1) represents to investors/potential investors that it pursues a venture capital strategy; (2) immediately after acquisition of any asset (other than qualifying investments or short-term holdings) holds no more than 20% of capital in non-qualifying investments; (3) does not borrow/issue debt or provide guarantees or leverage in excess of 15% of aggregate capital (with limited short-term exceptions); (4) only issues securities that do not provide holders with rights to withdraw/redeem except in extraordinary circumstances; and (5) is not registered under section 8 and has not elected to be treated as a business development company under section 54.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes a category of certain pre-existing venture capital funds (criteria concerning representations to investors and limits on sales after specified dates). Contains multiple defined terms (committed capital, equity security, qualifying investment, qualifying portfolio company, reporting or foreign traded, short-term holdings) with detailed subtests used to determine qualification. Advisers may treat certain non-U.S. issuers as private funds if consistent with treatment under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private fund adviser exemption thresholds and conditions (§ 275.203(m)-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. investment advisers with principal office in the United States are exempt from registration if they (1) act solely as adviser to one or more qualifying private funds and (2) manage private fund assets of less than $150 million. Non-U.S. advisers are exempt if they have no client that is a United States person except qualifying private funds, and all assets managed at a U.S. place of business are solely attributable to private fund assets totaling less than $150 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private fund assets must be calculated annually per General Instruction 15 to Form ADV. Defines exclusions to assets under management for purposes of this exemption and provides related definitions (place of business, principal office and place of business, private fund assets, qualifying private fund, related person, United States, United States person) with notes on treatment of clients who change status.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC registration eligibility for mid-sized advisers and switching rules (§ 275.203A-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisers with AUM at least $100M but less than $110M may, but are not required to, register with the Commission; they need not withdraw registration unless AUM falls below $90M. Exceptions apply for advisers to registered investment companies or those eligible for specified exemptions. State-registered advisers must apply for SEC registration within 90 days of an annual updating amendment reporting eligibility; SEC-registered advisers who report they are no longer eligible must file Form ADV-W to withdraw within 180 days of fiscal year end. While registered with both, the Act and state law apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the registration buffer (100–110M) and withdrawal buffer (90M), timing requirements for switching to/from SEC registration, and consequences of overlapping registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from prohibition on Commission registration (§ 275.203A-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates circumstances where section 203A(a) prohibition does not apply: (a) pension consultants advising plans with aggregate value ≥ $200M (with aggregation rules); (b) advisers controlling/controlled by or under common control with a registered adviser when principal office is the same; (c) investment advisers expecting to be eligible for registration within 120 days and satisfying filing/withdrawal undertakings; (d) multi-state advisers required to register in 15 or more states who elect to rely on this paragraph and must maintain records of state determinations for five years; (e) internet investment advisers that provide advice exclusively through an operational interactive website and meet record-keeping and control restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies detailed eligibility and recordkeeping steps for each exemption (e.g., pension consultant aggregation method, required Schedule D representations, what constitutes an operational interactive website and 'digital investment advisory service').

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for SEC registration eligibility and representatives (§ 275.203A-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines key terms: (a) Investment adviser representative — a supervised person with more than five clients who are natural persons (excluding excepted persons) and more than 10% of whose clients are natural persons (excluding excepted persons), with exceptions for persons who do not regularly solicit/meet/communicate with clients or who provide only impersonal investment advice. (b) Place of business — an office at which the representative regularly provides advisory services and any other location held out to the public as such. (c) Principal office and place of business — executive office from which officers/partners/managers direct, control, and coordinate activities. (d) Assets under management — determined by calculating securities portfolios with continuous and regular supervisory or management services as reported on Form ADV. (e) State securities authority — the state's securities commissioner/commission or similar office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains cross-references and exceptions to help identify who counts as an adviser representative and what constitutes places of business for registration/eligibility purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to Form ADV — timing and electronic filing (§ 275.204-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must amend your Form ADV: (1) Parts 1 and 2 at least annually, within 90 days of fiscal year end, and more frequently if instructions require; (2) Part 3 at the frequency required by Form ADV instructions. Subject to hardship rules, all amendments to Part 1A, Part 2A, and Part 3 must be filed electronically with the IARD. If you have a continuing hardship exemption, file completed Part 1A, Part 2A and Part 3 on paper with the SEC by mailing to FINRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing fees: initial filing fee when first electronically filing Part 1A and an annual fee for each annual updating amendment; fees non-refundable and acceptance by FINRA depends on payment. Each amendment is a 'report' under sections 204 and 207. Transition rule: registered advisers prior to June 30, 2020 must electronically file initial Form CRS meeting Part 3 requirements beginning May 1, 2020 and no later than June 30, 2020. Notes on summaries of material changes and exhibit filing requirements.
